claims.value: Highest-value non-profile target: `analytics.home`. It had 16,389 canonical human pageviews over seven days, far above the other listed non-profile analytics families. Its prominent resources include `/in/playerActivity`, `/in/destiny2/telemetry/home`, `/in/destiny2`, and `/spa/telemetry/view`.

Recommended intervention: add useful HTTP/edge caching for the public analytics JSON responses, beginning with `/in/destiny2/telemetry/home`, and audit the other analytics-home resources for the same treatment. The client already fans out `GetAnalyticsHome` work with `Promise.all`, while APM says the telemetry-home endpoint is cheap when cached; RUM still pays network/payload time and the observed responses were Cloudflare `DYNAMIC` without useful cache-control. Lazy-load Pantheon on tab selection, or share/cache the collectibles response across raids and Pantheon. Keep the identity shell and let it render the ready scaffold early.

Prioritize the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. The evidence shows a high-volume endpoint with a near-instant cache-hit mode but 12–13 second p95 latency when requests rebuild activity data through Redis shard scans and math. Implement stale-while-revalidate with a longer stale TTL and a single background refresh lock so foreground requests never perform the rebuild.

Separately, change `/p/:identifier/raids` to render shell plus fast local raid statistics first, deferring Bungie collectible/progress enrichment. Pantheon should load only when selected, or reuse a shared cached `ProfileWCollectibles` result. These are evidence-backed proposals; the corpus does not show either change implemented or verified.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path. Seven-day RUM recorded 13,210 calls with p95 12.03 s, while APM recorded 23,255 spans with p75 2 ms but p95 13.03 s, indicating a frequent endpoint with a severe cache-miss tail. It also contributes to the high-traffic analytics-home fan-out.

Implement stale-while-revalidate for player activity: retain a longer-lived stale value, refresh it in the background under a single-flight/distributed lock, and prevent `apiPlayerActivity` requests from calling the expensive rebuild directly. The code-path reason is that `apiPlayerActivity` falls through from its cache to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`, while the five-minute sweeper cache has the same five-minute TTL; misses therefore expose Redis shard scanning and aggregation math to foreground traffic. Logs measured shard-scan p95 near 18 s and math p95 near 16 s.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie `ProfileWCollectibles` enrichment rather than local raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for all sources, the page remains in `RaidsLoading`, and raids plus eagerly requested Pantheon each fetch collectibles. Render the profile shell and fast local clears/full-clears/carries/fastest-run data first; defer collectible/progress enrichment, and lazy-load Pantheon on tab selection or share/cache one collectibles result across both endpoints.

After the player-activity change, compare RUM and APM count/average/p75/p95 for `/in/playerActivity`, foreground rebuild and shard-scan/math log counts and durations, analytics-home load/LCP, refresh concurrency, error rate, and activity-data age/freshness against the saved baseline. Obsidian and Markdown are prototype corpora, human-readable projections, and export formats; they are neither the canonical product boundary nor necessarily the canonical storage representation. The first benchmark was too narrow because it measured retrieval readiness over frozen questions and evidence items, and its best workspace result merely tied one-shot top-k on passed cases while recovering fewer evidence items at higher context cost. That historical result did not demonstrate the workspace hypothesis. The superseding evaluation gate must test fresh-agent continuation of real workloads, comparing direct filesystem tools, model-directed agent workspace calls, and fixed handoff packs. It must prove that an agent can resume, advance, iterate, compute, verify, reason about temporal changes and supersession, inspect full sources, and leave correct durable next-state artifacts. A blinded model-answer evaluation on an untouched holdout is required before choosing a canonical storage engine.

answer.answer: Safe implementation checkpoint: keep personal and work memories in physically separate instances. Automate only signed, encrypted, application-layer replication from the cloud-authoritative personal service, through a one-way outbox, into a read-only work importer and work-local replica. The importer must have no route, credential, or write capability for the personal service. Nothing work-derived—including queries, prompts, embeddings, outputs, telemetry, acknowledgements, logs, or derived state—may return through this channel. A work recommendation may enter personal context only after explicit human-reviewed declassification, followed by a separate personal-side versioned workspace write. The read-only retrieval interface and versioned workspace writes are distinct surfaces; read access must not imply authority to write personal memory. Exact service boundaries, keys, deletion receipts, telemetry controls, and assurance language remain unresolved, so this is an architecture checkpoint rather than a verified implementation.

The only allowed automated direction is personal to work: the personal cloud publishes signed, encrypted, versioned snapshots or deltas—including applicable deletion tombstones—to a dedicated neutral outbox; a read-only work importer consumes them and builds its replica and indexes locally.
